title: Neos Oikodomikos Kanonismos (NOK) - New Building Code

articles.title: Field of Application
articles.summary: Defines the scope of the building code. Applies to all construction within and outside city plans in Greece.

articles.title: Definitions
articles.summary: Defines key terms: building, floor, basement, semi-basement, attic, mezzanine, pilotis, etc.
key_rules: Building: any fixed construction above or below ground for human use
Floor height: measured from finished floor to finished floor above
Pilotis: open ground floor used for passage or parking

articles.title: Coefficients and Magnitudes
articles.summary: Defines coverage ratio, building factor, volume factor, building height, setbacks.
key_rules: Coverage ratio (syntelestis kalypsis): max ground floor area / plot area
Building factor (syntelestis domisis): max total building area / plot area
Building height: measured from natural or formed ground to highest point

articles.title: Building Permits
articles.summary: Categories of permits: building permit (oikodomiki adeia), notification of minor works, permission for small works.
key_rules: Building permit required for new buildings, additions, major renovations
Notification sufficient for internal modifications, minor repairs
Permit issued by local YPDOM (poleodomia) or via e-Adeies platform
Required documents: topographic diagram, architectural study, static study, MEP study

articles.title: Building Use
articles.summary: Classification of building uses: residential, commercial, industrial, special.
key_rules: Use must comply with zoning designation of the area
Mixed use permitted in mixed-use zones
Change of use requires permit if the category changes

articles.title: Protection of Heritage
articles.summary: Rules for buildings near monuments, traditional settlements, and protected areas.
key_rules: Ministry of Culture approval needed within archaeological zones
Special building conditions may apply in traditional settlements
Height and form restrictions near listed monuments

articles.title: Plot Viability and Buildability
articles.summary: Defines when a plot is artio (viable) and oikodomisimo (buildable).
key_rules: Within plan: plot must have minimum frontage on approved road, meet minimum area
Outside plan (ektos schediou): minimum 4000m2 (4 stremma) with 45m road frontage
Exceptions (parekklisi) for smaller plots: 750m2 with 10m frontage on provincial/national road, or plots existing before 1985 regulations
Plot must have legal access to approved road

articles.title: Special Cases of Buildability
articles.summary: Exceptions and special conditions for plot buildability.
key_rules: Plots existing before city plan approval may have reduced requirements
Corner plots may have different frontage requirements
Unified plots from land consolidation have special rules

articles.title: Easements on Properties
articles.summary: Building restrictions due to easements, rights of way, and infrastructure.
key_rules: Minimum distances from roads, railways, power lines
No building within road widening zones
Archaeological easements require Ministry approval

articles.title: Environmental Upgrade Incentives
articles.summary: Bonus building factor for energy-efficient buildings.
key_rules: Up to 10% bonus building factor for buildings exceeding energy requirements
Green roof bonus: additional coverage allowance
Pilot programs for net-zero buildings

articles.title: Building Factor (Syntelestis Domisis)
articles.summary: How total buildable area is calculated.
key_rules: Within plan: defined by city plan decree (FEK)
Outside plan residential: 0.40 for first 4000m2, 0.02 for rest, max 400m2
Outside plan agricultural/tourism: varies by use
Basement, pilotis, and certain common areas excluded from factor calculation

articles.title: Coverage Ratio
articles.summary: Maximum ground floor footprint as percentage of plot.
key_rules: Within plan: defined by city plan decree (FEK)
Outside plan: 10% of plot area for up to 4000m2
Additional structures (pools, pergolas) may have separate coverage allowances

articles.title: Volume Factor
articles.summary: Total volume of building relative to plot area.
key_rules: Applied in specific zones defined by city plans
Typically 3.0-5.0 times the building factor value

articles.title: Building Placement and Setbacks
articles.summary: Rules for positioning buildings on plots.
key_rules: Within plan: setbacks defined by city plan, typically 2.5-5m from boundaries
Outside plan: 15m from road axis, 5m from side boundaries
Buildings can be built on boundary in specific urban zones (systima syneches domisis)
Distance between buildings on same plot: min 2.5m per side (total gap >= 5m)

articles.title: Building Height
key_rules: Within plan: defined by city plan decree, typically 7.5m-32m
Outside plan: max 7.5m (2 floors) for residential
Height measured from highest natural or formed ground at building perimeter
Mechanical rooms, chimneys, solar panels may exceed max height by 1.5-2.5m

articles.title: Number of Floors
key_rules: Determined by max height and minimum floor height (2.70m residential, 3.00m commercial)
Mezzanines count as floors if over 50% of floor area
Attic counts as floor if ceiling height exceeds 1.70m over 50% of area

articles.title: Semi-basements and Basements
key_rules: Semi-basement: ceiling max 1.50m above grade
Basement must have minimum ceiling height 2.40m
Basements excluded from building factor if used for parking/storage
Semi-basements with habitable use count toward building factor

articles.title: Building Outside City Plan (Ektos Schediou)
articles.summary: Specific rules for construction outside approved city plans.
key_rules: Min plot 4000m2 (4 stremma) with 45m frontage
Exception: 750m2 with 10m frontage near provincial road
Coverage: 10%
Building factor: 0.40 for first 4000m2, 0.02 for remainder
Max total building area: 400m2 for residential
Max height: 7.5m
Max floors: 2
Setback from road axis: 15m
Setback from boundaries: 5m
Must not be within forest map, archaeological zone, coastal setback, Natura 2000 unless specifically permitted

tourism.notes: Environmental impact assessment may be required. Special tourism zone rules may apply.
